reasons.A: Long, clause-heavy sentences and semicolons fit, but it stacks hedges (may be, I suspect, in some sense, arguably, it seems to me, perhaps) and bookends with rhetorical questions, thicker than the passage and so edging into caricature.
reasons.B: Closest match: long, balanced sentences with measured hedging ('I am not sure that conclusion survives'), a single dash-led list, semicolon-joined clauses and a restrained, reflective turn, without overdoing the mannerisms.
reasons.C: Short, punchy sentences, imperatives and a confident, advisory tone ('Catch them early and they stay small. Miss them and they grow.') are far from the passage's slow, hedged, essayistic movement.
